subject: Re: RFP bake-off timing — request for extra eval credits and window extension
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@clearmed.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: rfp@clearmed.ai
Date: 2028-09-12T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: RFP bake-off timeline / ask for more eval credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency numbers and the runtime features. We're running a three-vendor bake-off to inform our shortlist and the judges schedule shifted; the evaluation window now overlaps with an internal compliance audit.

Two asks: can you (1) top up our eval credits by 50% so we can run a second pass of throughput tests, and (2) extend the trial window by one additional week to accommodate the audit reschedule? The procurement team asked that we get any promotional approvals documented for their RFP packet.

I've attached the updated scope (ClearMed_RFP_scope_v3.pdf) for reference.

Best,
Evan Brooks
Head of ML Ops — ClearMed Health
E: evan.brooks@clearmed.ai
T: +1 415-555-0192

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off timeline / ask for more eval credits

Hi Evan — appreciate the heads-up and the updated scope. Happy to try to make this work. A couple quick notes before I loop in my manager and ops:

- Can you confirm the current credit balance and the expected token/embeddings volume for the second pass? If you can share the rough runbook (e.g., full-batch encoding + 10k generation tokens per test), that helps us size the top-up.
- Is the extension strictly for one extra week, or do you want a firm calendar end date?

I'll tag Neha and Ben on the cc for ops and commercial guidance and get internal approval. If we can document this as an RFP-specific promotional adjustment (conditions: usage only for ClearMed RFP tests, expires 30 days after the extended window), we should be able to escalate.

I'll follow up today with a formal approval path.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@clearmed.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-12T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off timeline / ask for more eval credits

Thanks Rishi — quick answers below:

- Current balance: ~420k token-equivalent credits remaining (from the initial sandbox allocation).
- Expected extra consumption: approx 250k token-equivalent for the second pass across 3 model families (generation + reranking + embeddings).
- Extension: one week beyond current end date is sufficient; prefer an explicit calendar end: extend from 2028-09-24 to 2028-10-01.

If it's helpful we can mark the top-up and extension as "RFP-only" in paperwork; procurement wants a short note they can include in the submission.

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Evan

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@clearmed.ai>
Date: 2028-09-13T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP bake-off timeline / ask for more eval credits — approval request

Marissa — forwarding ClearMed's request. Short summary: prospect on an active RFP asking for a 50% eval credit top-up (~210k token-equivalent) and a one-week trial extension to 2028-10-01. They will use it strictly for a controlled bake-off; procurement needs documented approval for the RFP packet.

Why this is important: ClearMed is a strong strategic healthcare account (compliance requirements + potential Dedicated pilot). If we can accommodate under a conditional promo, we increase chances of getting to preferred-vendor shortlist.

Asks: 1) approval to grant 210k token-equivalent credit top-up as an RFP promo, expiring 2028-10-31 (30 days after extended window); 2) approve trial window extension to 2028-10-01; 3) confirm any logo/PR constraints.

I'm tagging Ben for pricing guidance and Jordan to ensure ops logs the credit in the deal and that we create a HubSpot note (link below). Evan is included for transparency. I can draft the approval memo if you want.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/deal/12345

Thanks — Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-09-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP bake-off timeline / ask for more eval credits — approval request

Thanks for the context, Rishi. I approve the following on a case-by-case RFP promo basis:

1) Grant 210k token-equivalent top-up to ClearMed as a one-time promotional credit.
2) Extend their sandbox/trial window to 2028-10-01.
3) Conditions: credits are RFP-only; usage must be limited to the models and scopes listed in ClearMed_RFP_scope_v3.pdf; credit expires 2028-10-31.
4) No public PR or co-marketing without a separate signed agreement — procurement can include a redacted approval note in their RFP packet.
5) Require Sales Ops to record the promo as "RFP: ClearMed — promo credit" in HubSpot and attach the approval spreadsheet.

Ben/Jordan/Neha — please action the technical allocation and HubSpot entry. Rishi — please send the confirmation language to Evan and attach the approval sheet for procurement.

Marissa Cole

Evan — good news. Management approved the RFP promotional adjustment. Summary of the approved items below (please quote this in your procurement submission):

- Promo top-up: 210,000 token-equivalent credits added to ClearMed sandbox.
- Trial extension: sandbox window extended to 2028-10-01 (inclusive).
- Credit expiry: any unused promotional credits expire 2028-10-31.
- Conditions: credits are granted for RFP evaluation only; usage must adhere to the model/scope in the attached ClearMed_RFP_scope_v3.pdf; no public co-marketing without a separate agreement.

I've CC'd Sales Ops (Jordan) and Commercial Ops (Ben) — Jordan will log the promo in HubSpot and Ben will record the pricing note. Attached approval sheet is the official internal record.

Next steps for us: Jordan will confirm allocation (should reflect in your console by EOD tomorrow) and I'll check in mid-week on how the second pass looks. If you need any expanded model variants for latency stress tests we can discuss quant and batching setups.

Thanks, and good luck with the second pass.

Best,
